DOI:10.1109/aiita69518.2026.11567036.abstract: Large language models perform strongly on many language and reasoning benchmarks yet it remains unclear whether these successes reflect stable internal world models or mainly local pattern continuation. We study this question in a structured navigation setting by proposing a formal evaluation framework grounded in deterministic finite automata (DFA) and the Myhill-Nerode theorem. We map the Beijing subway to a minimal DFA and evaluate Chinese LLMs with four complementary tasks: Next-Token prediction for local transition validity, Sequence Compression for merging history-equivalent states, Sequence Distinction for detecting state boundaries, and Detour Fragility for state updating and replanning under perturbations. Across five mainstream Chinese commercial models, local next-step prediction is substantially stronger than global state reasoning. Models often fail to compress distinct histories that correspond to the same state, miss discriminative boundaries at transfer nodes, and rarely recover after a forced detour. The results suggest that current behavior is driven more by local trajectory continuation than by stable abstraction of environmental state. Our framework offers a formal and reproducible way to quantify structural consistency and provides a practical lens for assessing world-model claims in language models.

DOI:10.1109/ainit61980.2024.10581858.abstract: In today's society, multivariate time series classification has wide-ranging applications, such as action recognition, health monitoring, and so on. In recent years, with the breakthrough progress of transformer networks based on self-attention mechanism in various fields, their powerful long sequence modeling ability has also shown good performance in time series classification tasks. However, present transformer networks utilized for multivariate time series classification predominantly encode the values of all variables at each timestamp as inputs to the encoder, aimed at computing dependencies between temporal steps. This practice often neglects certain dynamic features inherent in time series data, such as periodicity. In response to this limitation, the present study introduces a multi-scale feature fusion transformer (MFformer), a model that employs the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to ascertain periods with the most significant influence and divides the original time series data into subsequences according to these periods for input into the transformer network, thereby capturing dependencies among periods. To extract temporal features within these periods, MFformer replaces the feadforward layer in the original transformer with two convolutional layers. Concurrently, MFformer adopts a flow-attention mechanism in lieu of the traditional self-attention mechanism to achieve a lower temporal complexity. Finally, a gating mechanism is employed to integrate features from subsequences of different scale. The efficacy of the proposed approach is demonstrated through validation on eight publicly available datasets.

DOI:10.1109/ainit65432.2025.11035140.abstract: Generating relevant and diverse responses remains challenging for non-pretrained small models in open-domain multi-turn dialogues. To address the one-to-many mapping problem caused by conversational uncertainty, we propose a novel framework integrating Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model. The VAE component learns three distinct latent variables: background, roles, and topic, to capture dynamic conversational factors, while the MoE module employs context-aware gating to dynamically activate domain-specific experts based on these variables. Extensive experiments on multi-turn dialogue datasets show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art non-pretrained baselines, particularly in improving the relevance and diversity of responses.

DOI:10.1109/aiot66900.2025.00075.abstract: Multi-user environments present significant challenges in coordinating diverse preferences and resolving conflicts around shared resources. Single-agent systems struggle to balance individual needs with collective objectives. We introduce MALLM, a novel framework that deploys personalized LLM-based agents for each user on edge devices, which integrates multi-sensor data fusion with a structured multi-agent decision-making mechanism, processing all data locally for enhanced privacy. Our edge-computing architecture enables real-time deliberation through evidence-based argumentation and consensus formation algorithms. The system continuously refines user profiles through sensor data while managing computational resources efficiently. We evaluate MALLM in a real-world 30-day deployment with four users, demonstrating 87.3% user satisfaction compared to 62.5% for majority voting approaches, while achieving 94.1% safety scores and 91.7% adaptability.

DOI:10.1109/airc64931.2025.11077480.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive technical framework for constructing effective multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs). We examine how multiple LLM-based agents can collaborate to solve complex problems beyond the capabilities of single agents through specialized knowledge integration and optimized communication protocols. Our novel architecture enables efficient collaboration between heterogeneous LLM agents, each with domain-specific capabilities and knowledge bases. Experimental results demonstrate that our multi-agent LLM system achieves 42% higher accuracy on complex knowledge tasks, 37% reduction in hallucinations, and 29% faster convergence on collaborative problem-solving compared to baseline approaches. By implementing optimized knowledge retrieval mechanisms and structured communication patterns, our system reduces token usage by 45% while maintaining semantic fidelity across agent interactions. These findings establish key design principles for building more effective and reliable collaborative LLM-based multi-agent systems for enterprise applications

DOI:10.1109/amlds63918.2025.11159345.abstract: Brain tumor segmentation on MRI is a critical task in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight network based on the U-Net architecture—3D IDC-MambaUNet. This model integrates Inception Depthwise Convolution (IDC) blocks with a U-Mamba bottleneck and employs a multi-resolution fusion strategy to effectively capture multi-scale features. Specifically, we combine a low-resolution model designed to capture global features with a full-resolution model that extracts local details, thereby integrating broad and local information simultaneously. This approach significantly improves the detection and segmentation of brain tumor lesions. Experiments on a brain tumor MRI dataset demonstrate that, compared to conventional benchmark models, our method achieves higher lesion-level F1 scores and Dice coefficients while significantly reducing the model parameters and inference time. Overall, these results indicate that our model strikes an excellent balance between high segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, making it highly suitable for real-time clinical deployment.

DOI:10.1109/apsec66846.2025.00099.abstract: The current Retrieval-Augmented Generation(RAG) pipeline incorporates retrieved contexts as external knowledge to reduce hallucinations, but the large and redundant context makes it difficult for the model to identify key information. In Question-Answering (QA) tasks, large language models (LLMs) can identify query-focused information through extractive compression, simplify redundant long texts and improve the accuracy, but they are resource-intensive and less efficient. To ensure the accuracy of extractive compression and improve its efficiency, we propose a framework for query-focused extractive compression (QEC-LLM) that leverages the LLM’s knowledge and a queryguided mechanism to construct sample sets, effectively training a smaller student model. The student model sorts and scales paragraph sentences based on similarity scores for compression and performance optimization. In addition, since LLM may generate some information that is missing from the student model during the extraction process, our framework will add this supplementary information to the QA prompt and combine it with the extracted information to achieve generative augmentation. We conduct extensive experiments on QA datasets with different compression ratios. The results demonstrate that QECLLM significantly improves end-to-end QA performance and inference efficiency, while demonstrating strong generalization across different retrieval strategies.

DOI:10.1109/apsipaasc58517.2023.10317271.abstract: In the speech communication over the internet, due to the latency and jitter of the network, the data packets may be lost and result in a degraded user experience. Therefore, the packet loss concealment (PLC) technology plays an important role in recovering the lost information. In this paper, a PLC method only using few historical information is proposed based on generative adversarial network (GAN). In this method, the generator is composed of the improved gated attention unit (IGAU) and temporal convolution network, which can fully exploit the available time-domain information and recover the lost speech signal. Specially, a consistent mapping approach is devised to enhance the quality of the generated speech. In addition, two additional loss functions are used to assist in the training of network. The experimental results show that the proposed method has better performance in terms of both perceptual quality and speech intelligibility at different packet loss rates.

DOI:10.1109/asp-dac66049.2026.11420537.abstract: This paper presents NetTLM-DSE, a novel framework for exploring the design space of layer-pipeline spatial mapping (LP-SM) for a large-scale accelerator network based on SystemC transaction-level modeling (TLM). In detail, the proposed SystemC-TLM simulator, NetTLMSim, is used to predict the network delay and optimize the mapping of deep neural network (DNN) layers to multiple accelerator cores. Conventional analytical delay models fail to accurately predict the delay of a large-scale accelerator network because of lack of the ability to capture the dynamic traffic of an accelerator network such as network contention. Such inaccurate delay prediction makes it difficult to find the optimal or near-optimal LP-SM in the corresponding design space exploration (DSE). In contrast, NetTLMSim reduces the prediction error by up to 52.8% through its cycle-accurate modeling of dynamic traffic in accelerator networks. When applied to the DSE for Transformer LP-SM, the proposed cycle-accurate simulator can find the optimal or near-optimal design options more efficiently than the conventional analytical delay models. Specifically, the proposed DSE framework, NetTLM-DSE, is shown to achieve up to 37.8% lower delay than the conventional DSE framework. In addition, a set of simulated annealing (SA) operators using dynamic traffic profiles is newly proposed to improve the efficiency of DSE. In detail, it is shown that, when applied to the DSE for Transformer LP-SM, the proposed SA operators improve the DSE speed by up to $684 \times$ over conventional SA operators. The NetTLM-DSE is open-sourced at https://github.com/SDL-KU/NetTLM-DSE

DOI:10.1109/asru57964.2023.10389645.abstract: In this paper, we explore various frame rate reduction schemes on the two-pass cascaded encoder model to improve its efficiency without scarifying the transcription quality. We conduct extensive studies on frame rate reduction strategies, left and right context window length, trade-offs in quality, latency, computation and power consumption, and performance in short-and long-form datasets. With the proposed schemes, we can lower the 2nd pass frame rate to $120 \mathrm{~ms}$, half of the 1st pass’s. This achieves $20 \%$ RTF reduction / $13 \%$ power saving / $19 \%$ lower final latency, without impact on the word-error-rate nor partial results’ latency. If allowing partial latency increase, we can further reduce the frame rate to $180 \mathrm{~ms}$ or even $240 \mathrm{~ms}$ from the 1st pass, and obtain $45 \%$ RTF / 35% power savings, with a similar or even better (on the short-form testset) recognition accuracy.

DOI:10.1109/bci65088.2025.10931412.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals, widely used in neuroscience and clinical research, provide non-invasive insights into brain activity. However, their high variability, noise, and complex spatiotemporal dynamics present significant challenges for effective modeling. To tackle these issues, we introduce an energy-guided topology for EEG signal analysis within the Mamba framework, designed to enhance feature propagation by leveraging spectral energy distribution. Our method first transforms EEG signals into the frequency domain and constructs an energy-based topology using channel-wise spectral power. Features are then propagated bidirectionally along energy gradients, enabling the Mamba model to capture temporal and spatial dependencies more effectively. By aligning feature learning with energy flow in the frequency domain, our approach improves the efficiency and accuracy of EEG modeling. Experimental results on the public dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms CNN-based, Transformer-based, and vanilla Mamba models, underscoring its potential to advance EEG signal processing.

DOI:10.1109/bibm62325.2024.10822091.abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) emerged as a promising, non-invasive, real-time, high-resolution imaging technology for cervical cancer detection. The scarcity of high-quality annotated cervical OCT images severely hinders the predictive performance of deep learning models. In contrast, self-supervised learning (SSL) methods offer a viable solution to the above challenge. This study aims to develop a cost-effective SSL framework that efficiently classifies high-resolution cervical OCT images to meet the clinical "see-and-diagnose" requirement for cervical lesions. Therefore, we propose COVE, a novel SSL framework with masked autoencoders based on VMamba with linear complexity. To our knowledge, COVE is the first SSL framework using masked image modeling for VMamba to leverage large unlabeled cervical OCT datasets. It has two specific designs: (1) 2D-Selective-Scan for visible patches (VP-SS2D): the VMamba encoder’s core module processes only visible patches for efficient pre-training and addressing the inconsistency between pre-training and fine-tuning; (2) visible patch feature-preserving (VPFP): visible patch features in each decoder block are replaced with encoder-extracted features, decoupling the encoder’s feature extraction from the decoder’s pixel reconstruction tasks. Experimental results showed that COVE outperformed existing SSL frameworks in five-fold cross-validation on a 1,452-subject cervical OCT dataset from a multi-center study and two external validation sets from top Chinese hospitals. Additionally, COVE demonstrated the highest pre-training efficiency, with significantly faster speed than existing SSL frameworks.

DOI:10.1109/bibm66473.2025.11356369.abstract: Deep learning models, due to their strong capabilities in learning from data and representing features, have been widely deployed, particularly in the medical field. However, given the limitations of medical devices and deployment scenarios, more and more researchers are focusing on how to better deploy deep learning models on resource-constrained edge devices to enable real-time medical data analysis. Nevertheless, such resourceconstrained IoT devices present significant challenges, making it difficult to achieve both high accuracy and low inference latency. To address this problem, we propose a novel framework, RC-DLM, designed to split and execute complex deep learning models on IoT devices. Specifically, we partition a deep learning model into multiple sub-models according to the computational capacity of each device, with each sub-model responsible for handling a subset of classes. To further reduce computation overhead and inference latency, we integrate a class-wise pruning method to shrink the size of each sub-model. Through large-scale experiments conducted on four popular datasets with three model architectures, we demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces inference latency and model size by up to 5.72 times and 57.5 times, respectively. We further deploy our method on real-world edge devices and compare it with state-of-theart approaches, evaluating the three most important aspects: accuracy, inference time, and model size. The comprehensive experimental results of our RC-DLM confirm the effectiveness of our proposed method.

DOI:10.1109/bibm66473.2025.11356901.abstract: To address the lack of explicit modeling for the multi-level reasoning process of “syndrome differentiation → treatment principle → prescription” in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), this paper proposes a two-stage, chain-ofthought (CoT) driven training framework for large language models. The approach is applied to the tasks of prescription generation and proprietary Chinese medicine (PCM) recommendation for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A dualpath reasoning dataset is constructed based on the logical sequence of “symptom → pathogenesis → treatment method → formula,” followed by two-stage fine-tuning: the first stage supervises the reasoning process explicitly, while the second stage optimizes clinical adaptability using real-world medical records. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves performance improvements of 1.2 % and 6.1 % over the baseline, with expert evaluations indicating significantly enhanced scores. These findings validate the effectiveness of explicit CoT supervision and the two-stage training strategy in improving the reasoning consistency and clinical applicability of TCM medication decision-making.

DOI:10.1109/bibm66473.2025.11357013.abstract: Medical object detection plays a vital role in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), enabling automatic and precise localization of lesions from medical images. In recent years, the YOLO series has been widely adopted as a mainstream real-time detection architecture. However, its commonly used Path Aggregation Feature Pyramid Network (PAFPN) still shows limitations in spatial modeling and fine-grained perception under low-contrast images. Meanwhile, State Space Models (SSMs), with their linear complexity and excellent long-range dependency modeling capability, have demonstrated great potential in both sequential modeling and vision tasks. To this end, this paper proposes a lightweight medical object detection framework dubbed MedMamba-YOLO, which integrates state-space modeling and multi-scale structural awareness. In this framework, we construct a Multi-Scale Fusion FPN (MSF-FPN) and embed a newly designed Spatial-Aware Visual State Space Block (SAVSSB) to achieve efficient cross-scale semantic interaction and contextual modeling. A Cross Path Interaction Block (CPIB) is also devised to strengthen feature representation via cross-path interactions and residual enhancement. Furthermore, a Heterogeneous Multi-scale Dilated Attention Detection Head (HMDADetect) is designed to adaptively model objects at different scales through a multi-branch variable dilation mechanism. Experiments conducted on the Br35H and BCCD datasets demonstrate that MedMamba-YOLO with only 3.8M parameters and 8.8GFLOPs achieves state-of-the-art performance without the need for pretraining. The source codes are publicly available at: https://github.com/HHH-JYG/MedMamba-YOLO.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata50022.2020.9378470.abstract: With the advent of big data, training deep learning models quickly has gained prime significance. The faster a model is trained, the more relevant are its predictions in a given context. Deep learning is used for non structured data such as images, videos, sounds, text corpus, all of which represent a huge volume of data and also use complex models. Training these workloads can often take days or even weeks, because of various factors such as size of data, complexity of model, network and the underlying hardware infrastructure. The recognized divide and conquer solution to expedite the training process is to distribute either data or the model. Alas, the challenges of a distributed training setup are well known - creating and maintaining a cluster, enabling data or model parallelism along with uninterrupted communication across the cluster nodes.In this paper, we focus on two lightweight libraries for distributed deep learning, RaySGD and Horovod, which aim to alleviate these challenges by providing support for seamless parallellization. We conduct an in-depth benchmarking exercise to evaluate the performance of both libraries for training time(latency) incurred. Our experiments are conducted on a combination of various parameters such as hardware setup (CPU or GPU based), standard and manually coded models, real world and synthetic datasets. We also vary batch sizes of large workloads and number of worker nodes in a distributed setting. The insights obtained from our experiments act as guidelines for data scientists, facilitating the decision making process when conducting distributed training of big data applications on RaySGD or Horovod.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825010.abstract: Sampling is a fundamental problem in optimization, machine learning and theoretical computer science. A common region of interest for sampling is the polytope, which is defined by a set of linear inequalities. The algorithm that is sampling from polytopes usually requires heavy matrix algebra, including matrix multiplication, matrix inversion and matrix determinant. In this work, we show how to implement the heavy matrix algebra in the area of sampling in nearly linear time for the polytope that has small treewidth. In particular, given a polytope defined by a matrix A ∈ ℝn×d with treewidth τ, we improve the running time of each iteration for three typical sampling algorithms for polytopes such as Dikin Walk, Soft-Threshold Dikin Walk and Vaidya Walk from O(nd2) to O(nτ2) by exploiting the small treewidth structures of the matrices.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825869.abstract: We consider a supervised classification problem of categorizing e-commerce products based on just the words in the title. If done in real-time, the categorization can greatly benefit sellers by enabling them to offer immediate feedback. We present a deterministic algorithm by constructing weighted word co-occurrence graphs from the listing/item titles. We empirically evaluate this algorithm on two publicly available product listing datasets, Etsy and Amazon. Our method’s accuracy is comparable to that of a supervised classifier constructed using the fastText library. The inference time of our model is up to 2.9× faster than the fastText classifier and has small training times. The training and inference of our model scales well for big datasets performing large-scale classification on millions of listings. We perform a detailed analysis and provide insights into our method and the product categorization task.

DOI:10.1109/bigdata66926.2025.11400819.abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have sparked an agentic revolution, transforming static language generation models into dynamic, autonomous agents capable of performing sophisticated, multi-step reasoning tasks. Our research introduces a novel multi-agent architecture leveraging LLMs to autonomously interpret user queries, generate structured execution plans, interact with NoSQL databases such as Amazon DynamoDB, generate answers, and validate query results. Our system addresses fundamental challenges in NoSQL querying, including schema variability, index selection complexity, limited native filtering capabilities, context window constraints, and hallucination risks. Central to our methodology is a four-agent framework - “Planner,” “Executor”, “Answer Generator,” and “Judge” - with the latter implementing a novel triple-model consensus mechanism that significantly enhances result accuracy and consistency. Empirical validation demonstrates our approach achieves 95% accuracy for the most complex queries on a diverse benchmark comprising 1,000 movie related questions across four complexity levels, significantly outperforming conventional retrieval methods by $20-25 \%$. Through comprehensive studies and error analysis, we establish a foundation for scalable, reliable querying of semi-structured data stores. Our results open new paths toward autonomous query planning, data retrieval, and result verification in large-scale, semi-structured databases.

DOI:10.1109/bigdia71496.2026.11684597.abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for autonomous driving commonly encode multi-camera images and navigation text into a single dense output token and decode it directly into a trajectory. This one-step, stateless mapping conflates tactical intent with operational control, exposes no explicit, differentiable intermediate state that a downstream module can supervise or inspect, and cannot anticipate future intent without re-invoking the heavyweight vision-language backbone. We propose WorldIntent, a framework that routes this output through a structured belief state rather than decoding it in a single step. A Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) maintains the belief state from the stream of VLM outputs and action feedback, and three supervised decoders read lateral, longitudinal, and safety intent from it. The belief state and the decoded intent jointly condition a trajectory planner whose action feeds back into the next transition, closing a state-action loop in the decision space. The same transition supports three inference modes from shared parameters: posterior recognition that incorporates the VLM output, prior prediction without it, and prior-rollout imagination that anticipates future intent without re-invoking the frontend. On Bench2Drive, WorldIntent is competitive with discriminative baselines on intent recognition and leads on lateral intent. As the only compared model with a generative prior, it anticipates about 83% of should-brake events one step ahead through prior-rollout imagination.

DOI:10.1109/bts-i2c63534.2024.10942193.abstract: The limited English proficiency in Indonesia, ranked 79th globally according to the English Proficiency Index (EPI), creates significant barriers in accessing global opportunities across education, business, and technology. Machine Translation (MT), particularly Neural Machine Translation (NMT), has emerged as a promising solution to overcome such linguistic challenges. This study explores the impact of hyperparameter optimization on translation accuracy in models deployed on edge devices, such as the Raspberry Pi Zero, which have limited computational power and memory. A Transformer-based NMT model was developed and trained using the Tatoeba dataset, consisting of English-Indonesian sentence pairs. The primary focus was on optimizing four key hyperparameters: the number of layers (num_layers), model dimension (d_model), feed-forward dimension (dff), and the number of attention heads (num_heads). Eight different scenarios were designed to evaluate how variations in these hyperparameters affect both the model's translation accuracy, measured by the BLEU score, and the execution time on the edge device. The results reveal a trade-off between model accuracy and execution time. While higher values of num_layers, d_model, and num_heads led to improved BLEU scores, they also significantly increased the execution time, sometimes making the model impractical for real-time applications on devices with limited resources. Conversely, configurations with lower hyperparameter values were more efficient in terms of execution time but at the cost of reduced translation accuracy. The findings underscore the importance of carefully balancing hyperparameter settings to achieve a model that is both accurate and efficient on edge devices. This study provides valuable insights for developers aiming to deploy deep learning models on low-power hardware, emphasizing the need for strategic hyperparameter optimization in such constrained environments.

DOI:10.1109/c366505.2025.11340545.abstract: Early detection of firearms in urban environments is a critical component of modern public security systems, enabling the anticipation of risk situations and the mitigation of criminal and violent acts. Traditional video surveillance systems face significant limitations, such as the need for continuous human supervision, low real time response capacity, and poor scalability across multiple critical zones. In this context, we propose a firearm detection model based on deep learning techniques optimized for low power devices through the use of Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) and Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI). This solution enables on device inference, reducing latency and dependence on cloud computing infrastructure. The system was implemented and evaluated on embedded platforms such as the Sipeed Maixduino and Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, integrating quantized convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures trained with firearm image datasets in diverse contexts. As a result, the MobileNet7_5 architecture was trained, achieving precision, recall, and F1-Score metrics of $0.98,0.94$, and 0.96, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of edge based video surveillance. This approach fosters the development of scalable, autonomous, and cost effective solutions for smart cities, aligned with principles of energy efficiency and proactive surveillance.

DOI:10.1109/cai68641.2026.11536381.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) perform strongly on many NLP tasks, yet their reliability on formal temporal reasoning remains unclear. We present a formally grounded evaluation framework for the past-time fragment of Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) that measures an LLM’s ability to interpret and reconstruct temporal constraints with semantic fidelity. The pipeline integrates constraint-guided synthesis, automata-theoretic verification, symbol-free obfuscation, grammar-constrained reconstruction, and counterexample-driven repair within a unified loop. Equivalence is checked via language inclusion, and shortest counterexamples provide graded feedback. The experiments across five instruction-tuned models (LLAMA-3.2-1B, QWEN2.5-7B, GEMMA-3-4B, DEEPSEEK-MATH-7B, MATHSTRAL-7B) show a consistent positive association between fidelity and understanding for the obfuscator, and a monotone relationship between fidelity and intelligence for the player. Covariance analysis indicates that variability is higher for the player, suggesting that reconstruction behavior contributes more to performance variance than obfuscation. This highlights the significance of improving grammar-constrained decoding, CKB-guided beam scoring, and counterexample-driven repair, which deliver larger gains than refining obfuscation alone. The framework provides a reproducible basis for diagnosing and improving temporal reasoning in LLMs.

DOI:10.1109/cain66642.2025.00015.abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is increasingly employed in building Generative AI applications, yet their evaluation often relies on manual, trial-and-error processes. Automating this evaluation process involves generating test data to trigger failures involving context comprehension, data formatting, specificity, and content completeness. Random question-answer generation is insufficient. However, prior works rely on standard QA datasets, benchmarks and tactics that are not tailored to the specific domain requirements. Hence, current approaches and datasets do not trigger sufficiently broad and context-specific failures. In this paper, we introduce evaluation scenarios that describe the process of generating question-answer pairs from content indexed by RAG pipelines, and they are designed to trigger a wider range of failures and to simplify automation. This enables developers to identify and address weaknesses more effectively. We validate our approach on five open-source RAG pipelines using three datasets. Our approach triggers high failure rates, by generating prompts that combine multiple questions (up to 91% failure rate) highlighting the need for developers to prioritize handling such queries. We generated failure rates of 60% in an academic domain dataset and 53% and 64% in open-domain datasets. Compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, our approach triggers 77% more failures on average per RAG pipeline and 53% more failures on average per dataset, offering a mechanism to support developers to improve the RAG pipeline quality.

DOI:10.1109/case56687.2023.10260565.abstract: We propose a dual-stream, semi-supervised, attention-based approach that employs feature fusion of RGB and Laser Range Finder (LRF) modalities. Our method lever-ages the strength of two powerful transformer-based networks, i.e. Vision Transformer (ViT) and SegFormer, along with LRF information, to adequately predict whether the scene encountered in the image is safe for a robot to traverse. Towards this effort, we introduce an automated labelling system profiting from the combination of raw velocity readings and laser scanning information. Moreover, we show that overall GOINO-GO detection is enhanced by fusing RGB and laser modalities. Feature fusion is achieved through the employment of a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) module. Through cross-domain validation, we show that the proposed traversability estimation method can achieve decent amounts of transferability even with limited amount of training data.

DOI:10.1109/cbase67452.2025.11335561.abstract: Real-time machine learning (ML) inference is increasingly deployed in latency-critical applications such as mobile computing, Internet-of-Things (IoT), and autonomous systems. However, existing inference frameworks typically rely on statically optimized kernels, which fail to adapt to dynamic workload variations and heterogeneous hardware conditions. This paper presents Dynamic Kernel Selection (DKS), a runtime framework that adaptively selects operator kernels during inference to optimize latency and energy efficiency. DKS integrates a lightweight profiler and decision engine that dynamically chooses among diverse kernel implementations, including precision variants (FP32, FP16, INT8), algorithmic strategies (GEMM, Winograd), and heterogeneous devices (CPU, GPU, edge accelerators). Experimental results on convolutional and transformer models (ResNet50, MobileNetV3, BERT) show that DKS achieves up to 38.2\% reduction in latency and $27.5 \%$ improvement in energy efficiency compared to state-of-the-art static baselines, while remaining within $5-7 \%$ of oracle performance. These findings highlight kernel-level adaptivity as a practical and scalable solution for efficient real-time ML inference across diverse platforms.

DOI:10.1109/ccgrid64434.2025.00057.abstract: As data volumes have grown, they offer opportunities to extract insights from them. The class of datasets we consider are spatiotemporal i.e., data that have spatial and temporal dimensions associated with them. In this study, we describe our methodology to support distributional similarity analysis at scale. Such distributional analyses are critical in identifying overall trends in spatiotemporally evolving phenomena, and can be used to inform model calibration and decision making. Our methodology leverages a mix of statistical, algorithmic, and systems approaches to facilitate effective analyses over voluminous datasets. We profile several aspects of our methodology, and our benchmarks validate several of our design choices.

DOI:10.1109/ccmcc67628.2025.11380739.abstract: DRAM caches are a well-known measure in order to increase the lifetime of established and emerging Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) technologies. However, a lot of these DRAM cache designs come at great additional cost, as conventional DRAMs, including their standards, are designed to function as main memory rather than a cache. Particularly, the management of the tag to identify cache entries as well as the cache flags marking invalid or modified entries is often dealt with by storing this cache metadata in-line, thus requiring additional memory accesses. Introduced with the novel LPDDR6 standard, a new extension featuring metadata along each payload, which the memory controller can use for any purpose of choice, can provide a solution for this issue. In this paper, we thus propose a DRAM cache leveraging LPDDR6, creating a fast and scalable DRAM cache with low implementation costs. By comparing our approach with a traditional DRAM cache design using the previous generation standard LPDDR5, not featuring the metadata extension, we can reduce energy consumption by up to 30% in real-world application scenarios.

DOI:10.1109/ceepe69795.2026.11552041.abstract: Provincial load forecasting is influenced not only by aggregated city-level demand but also by diverse external factors such as weather conditions, which increases modeling complexity. To address this issue, we propose an enhanced TimeXer-based framework for short-term provincial load forecasting by integrating temporal convolutional networks and a gated cross-attention mechanism. This design enables effective modeling of key dependencies between external variables and load dynamics while reducing noise interference. In addition, variational mode decomposition is employed to separate load signals into low-frequency trends and high-frequency fluctuations, allowing joint modeling of long-term patterns and short-term variations. Experiments on real load data from Hunan Province verify that the proposed method achieves superior forecasting accuracy compared with mainstream time-series models.

DOI:10.1109/cgo57630.2024.10444805.abstract: Computing gradients is a crucial task in many domains, including machine learning, physics simulations, and scientific computing. Automatic differentiation (AD) computes gradients for arbitrary imperative code. In reverse mode AD, an auxiliary structure, the tape, is used to transfer intermediary values required for gradient computation. The challenge is how to organize the tape in the memory hierarchy since it has a high reuse distance, lacks temporal locality, and inflates working set by 2-4×. We introduce Tapeflow, a compiler framework to orchestrate and manage the gradient tape. We make three key contributions. i) We introduce the concept of regions, which transforms the tape layout into an array-of-structs format to improve spatial reuse. ii) We schedule the execution into layers and explicitly orchestrate the tape operands using a scratchpad. This reduces the required cache size and on-chip energy. iii) Finally, we stream the tape from the DRAM by organizing it into a FIFO of tiles. The tape operands arrive just-in-time for each layer. Tapeflow, running on the same hardware, outperforms Enzyme, the state-of-the-art compiler, by 1.3-2.5×, reduces on-chip SRAM usage by 5–40 ×, and saves 8× on-chip energy. We demonstrate Tapeflow on a wide range of algorithms written in general-purpose language.

DOI:10.1109/cicc65509.2026.11509629.abstract: This paper presents a ROM-based LUT tensor engine that supports an output-stationary dataflow with an area-efficient complementary ROM structure, fully exploiting unstructured sparsity for fine-tuning-free ML inference. A latch-based PE efficiently exploits irregular zero patterns while avoiding redundant switching, minimizing energy for both dense and sparse inputs. The design achieves peak energy efficiency of 16.1 TOPS/W, outperforming prior LUT-based CIM macros and delivering 1.99× improvements compared to a state-of-the-art tensor engine.

DOI:10.1109/ciml69155.2026.11692785.abstract: Industrial knowledge graph (KG) construction for software engineering (SE) is often constrained by low-resource information extraction (IE), noisy user-generated text, and rapid domain evolution. We propose an Large Language Models (LLMs)-assisted framework that enables practical SE KG construction and maintenance with minimal supervision. Specifically, (1) the prompt-driven IE module first generates candidate triples via in-context learning (ICL) from a small labeled seed set; (2) these candidates are then filtered by a quality assurance pipeline using an LLM-as-a-judge strategy and refines the graph through embedding-based semantic deduplication; and (3) valid triples are finally integrated by a dynamic evolution mechanism that supports continuous updates through incremental adaptation and explicit version control of graph revisions. Experiments on three real-world SE corpora (CodeSearchNet, Stack Overflow, and GitHub Issues) show that LLM4SE-KG improves relation extraction F1 by 12.3–18.7% over strong baselines in our evaluation, while reducing end-to-end training cost by 40–60%. Ablation results demonstrate that prompt-based IE yields the largest gains, and that QA and evolution modules further improve consistency and robustness under noisy and shifting data. Overall, LLM4SEKG offers a scalable and low-supervision solution for industrial SE knowledge graphs.

DOI:10.1109/cisce69494.2026.11504855.abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition has attracted significant attention owing to its robustness to background variations and privacy-preserving properties. However, most existing methods model action sequences as undifferentiated continuous signals, overlooking the inherent stage-wise structure of human actions. This leads to suboptimal representations that conflate semantically distinct motion phases and are sensitive to redundant or corrupted frames. To address this issue, we propose the Adaptive Temporal Segmentation Transformer (AST), which explicitly and automatically discovers stage structure in a data-driven manner. AST learns temporal boundary points to partition sequences into semantically consistent segments, and introduces segment-aware positional encoding together with segment-constrained attention to capture both intra-stage dynamics and inter-stage relationships. Experiments on NTU RGB+D 60, NTU RGB+D 120, and NW-UCLA demonstrate competitive recognition accuracy alongside consistently improved robustness under Gaussian noise and joint-missing perturbations. It also shows stronger capability in modeling temporal structure. These results substantiate the value of structured temporal modeling for reliable skeleton-based action recognition.

DOI:10.1109/ciss63346.2024.11241166.abstract: Existing approaches for all-in-one weather removal often suffer from compromised image fidelity and prolonged inference durations. To this end, we introduce a dual-decomposed multi-scale parallel Transformer (DMPFormer) for restoring vision degraded by adverse weather conditions. Specifically, we develop a domain-decomposed feature enhancement mechanism (DFEM) to address issues arising from the self-attention mechanism in modeling high-frequency dependencies. DFEM decomposes features into spatial, wavelet and frequency domains, enabling more targeted and accurate feature learning. Meanwhile, we present a dimension-decomposed latent feature interaction module (DLFIM), which segregates features along height, width and channel dimensions, thereby optimizing feature fusion with multi-dimension mutual attention and adaptive determining weights. Besides, we propose a cross-scale implicit neural representation (CINR) for obtaining standardized representations of various degradations, which can adjustably provide visual prompts for subsequent reconstruction. Furthermore, we curate a comprehensive dataset containing diverse traffic weather-degraded image pairs. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our proposed model over existing approaches in both single and adverse weather removal.

DOI:10.1109/cloud72782.2026.00031.abstract: Efficient cluster scheduling requires reliable forecasts of resource demand, yet production workloads are heterogeneous, bursty, and strongly time-dependent. Using the Google Cluster-Usage Traces v3, we study leakage-safe prediction of three scheduling-relevant metrics: mean CPU demand, normalized memory pressure (average memory relative to assigned memory), and tail CPU demand (p95) as a burst-risk indicator. We develop a preprocessing and evaluation protocol that explicitly addresses two common threats to validity in trace-based learning: post-execution feature leakage (e.g., usage-derived fields) and identity leakage from random splits when recurring workloads appear in both training and test sets. Under time-ordered and gap-based splits, we compare gradient-boosted tree models (LightGBM) against strong history-only baselines (LastSeen and EMA) and perform a cold-start analysis by evaluating the first K occurrences of each workload entity. Results reveal a clear regime shift: for warm, recurring workloads, simple entity-history predictors achieve near-optimal accuracy and consistently outperform learned models; however, in cold-start settings where history is unavailable, LightGBM substantially improves CPU mean and tail forecasts (e.g., large gains in R2 for first-occurrence entities). These findings support a practical scheduling strategy: a hybrid, regime-aware policy that uses machine learning (ML) as a cold-start fallback and switches to lightweight history-based prediction as observations accumulate.

DOI:10.1109/cniot65435.2025.11070962.abstract: Forecasting of time series is vital in multiple sectors especially where precise predictions support decision-making. Transformer-Based models are widely favoured for their efficient self-attention mechanisms that effectively capture dependencies. Nonetheless, their quadratic complexity constrains scalability for extended sequences, resulting in the creation of sparse attention and external memory methods. To address these issues, we propose the Learnable Temporal Sparse Memory iTransformer (LTSMiTransformer), which integrates: Learnable Temporal Sparse Attention which dynamically identifies relevant time steps to reduce computational overhead; Memory-Augmented Module for capturing long-term dependencies without excessive memory consumption; and a Unified Embedding Strategy that enhances feature representation across heterogeneous datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LTSMiTransformer achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, particularly in long-horizon settings, while maintaining computational efficiency. Our analysis highlights its robustness to periodic patterns, trend shifts, and cross-domain adaptation. We also discuss limitations (e.g., hyper parameter sensitivity) and provide actionable insights for future work Codes available on GitHub.

DOI:10.1109/compsac65507.2025.00129.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and are now widely used in various applications globally. However, one of their major challenges is handling high-concurrency workloads, especially under extreme conditions. When too many requests are sent simultaneously, LLMs often become unresponsive which leads to performance degradation and reduced reliability in real-world applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes a queue-based system that separates request handling from direct execution. By implementing a distributed queue, requests are processed in a structured and controlled manner, preventing system overload and ensuring stable performance. This approach also allows for dynamic scalability, meaning additional resources can be allocated as needed to maintain efficiency. Our experimental results show that this method significantly improves resilience under heavy workloads which prevents resource exhaustion and enables linear scalability. The findings highlight the effectiveness of a queue-based web service in ensuring LLMs remain responsive even under extreme workloads.

DOI:10.1109/comst.2026.3681198.abstract: The growing complexity, scale, and heterogeneity of 6G wireless systems call for a shift toward AI-native architectures that are not only data-driven but also topology-aware, adaptive, and distributed. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), with their native support for graph-structured data, are well-suited for modeling the irregular and dynamic relationships inherent in wireless communication systems. However, standalone GNNs may be insufficient to address key 6G challenges such as continual learning, data scarcity, and dynamic adaptation. This survey, therefore, explores the emerging synergy between GNNs and complementary AI paradigms, including deep reinforcement learning (DRL), federated learning (FL), meta-learning, generative models, mixture-of-experts (MoE), and world models, enabling hybrid AI–GNN architectures for intelligent control, predictive adaptation, and scalable optimization across the wireless stack. We systematically review how these GNN-centric AI models can support intelligent functionality in next-generation network architectures such as O-RAN, as well as core 6G domains, including edge computing for wireless systems, advanced MIMO, traffic prediction, and digital twins. The survey also highlights key challenges in hybrid AI–GNN adoption, particularly scalability, generalization across dynamic topologies, interpretability, and symbolic reasoning, and discusses emerging strategies such as graph causality learning, dynamic GNNs, and neurosymbolic integration to address them. By consolidating recent advances and outlining open research directions, this work positions hybrid AI–GNN architectures as a promising approach toward enabling intelligent, energy-efficient, and context-aware wireless systems for 6G and beyond.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd64889.2025.11033237.abstract: Surface defect detection is widely used in various industrial scenarios. However, due to the characteristics of surface defects such as low contrast, blurry edges, and differences among individual defects, the detection task remains a significant challenge. Traditional semantic segmentation tasks based on Convolutional Neural Networks or Vision Transformers often underperform in establishing long-distance dependencies, while the latter suffers from high computational costs due to its complex second-order computations. Inspired by the Mamba state space model, we propose a high-resolution network (HMNet) based on the Mamba model. The main body of HMNet employs a special triangular structure, maintaining the size of the network output at 1/4 of the original image size, effectively focusing on the semantic features of fine-grained targets. We introduce the Contextual Mamba Block(CM Block) to construct the core sampling module within the encoder, aggregating positional information along both the horizontal and vertical directions based on the state space model, aiming to enhance the model's direction perception and global information fusion capabilities. We use experimental results from a private dataset of mobile phone glass screens and two publicly available datasets of surface defects on automotive parts and surface defects on hot rolled steel to demonstrate the effectiveness of HMNet for surface defect detection segmentation and its feasibility in industrial applications.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd64889.2025.11033534.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting has been widely used in many fields such as finance, electricity, etc., Transformer still plays an important role in multivariate time series research. However, most of the previous studies focus on the changes of the same variable in the time dimension and do not link the interactions among multivariate variables, which will make the prediction results inaccurate; meanwhile, capturing and extracting the features of the series only in the time domain will also ignore some hidden information. Therefore, we propose a Fourier Decomposition Transformer model with intra-inter variable Fourier dependencies(FFDFormer), which introduces a Fourier multi-kernel decomposition module to extract the obvious fluctuating seasonal components in the frequency domain, and then captures the long-term trend through a moving average kernel to model the different patterns. In addition, the model performs inter- and intra-variate feature extraction and introduces Fourier attention to capture more comprehensive serial information in the frequency domain. We conduct extensive experiments on six large datasets and show that the FFDFormer framework outperforms most existing benchmark models in terms of performance.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd64889.2025.11033589.abstract: Recommender systems are critical for mitigating information overload, assisting users in uncovering their latent interests, and enhancing their overall experience. Sequential recommendation leverages users' historical interaction sequences to predict dynamic interests more effectively than traditional rec-ommendation approaches. However, existing models-including RNN-based and Transformer-based methods-face significant limitations. RNNs struggle with vanishing gradients and long-term dependency capture, while Transformers, though effective for long-range relationships, suffer from computational inefficiency due to their quadratic attention complexity. Recent advancements have employed contrastive learning for sequential recommendation, aiming to enhance the consistency between augmented views and improve self-supervised learning signals. Despite their promise, these methods often lack diversity in data augmentation strategies, which restricts their capacity for bias mitigation, resulting in augmented data that still retains inherent biases. To address these challenges, we propose MDEC, a novel sequential modeling framework that leverages State Space Models (SSM) combined with unbiased contrastive learning. MDEC utilizes Mamba to efficiently model user preferences as an alternative to Transformer-based models. Additionally, it integrates graph-based information, including item transition and co-interaction data, to improve data augmentation comprehensively. Finally, we introduce adaptive anchor-enhanced contrastive learning, which adaptively utilizes augmented samples to improve representation quality and bias mitigation. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that MDEC significantly out-performs existing models, showcasing improved efficiency, better mitigation of biases, and enhanced recommendation quality. Code is available at https://github.com/Echohuangyan/CSLP.

DOI:10.1109/cscwd68734.2026.11582731.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) face a systemic vulnerability to automated jailbreak attacks, which mathematically exploit the deterministic nature of static inference configurations to optimize adversarial suffixes. Existing defense mechanisms—whether reliant on static alignment or reactive filtering—fail to effectively disrupt these gradient-based exploitations. To address this inherent defense-offense asymmetry, we propose RL-Shield, an endogenous Moving Target Defense (MTD) mechanism. By reformulating the passive decoding process into a sequential Markov Decision Process (MDP), RL-Shield acts as an active defense layer. We employ an integrated Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent that dynamically modulates continuous decoding hyperparameters (e.g., Temperature, Top-P) in real-time, guided by continuous semantic threat assessments. This dynamic hyperparameter adaptation introduces endogenous stochasticity, which severely destabilizes the attacker’s gradient landscape and exponentially increases the computational cost of convergence. Extensive evaluations across five diverse LLM architectures demonstrate that RL-Shield reduces the Attack Success Rate (ASR) by an average of 65.1% against state-of-the-art automated attacks while rigorously preserving the generation utility for benign queries. Our findings establish continuous hyperparameter modulation as a robust, lightweight, and deployment-ready defense paradigm against adaptive adversaries.

DOI:10.1109/csis-iac65538.2025.11162001.abstract: Anomaly detection of catenary support components (CSCs) is a crucial aspect of railway condition monitoring systems. However, because the abnormal features of CSC loosening are not immediately apparent, and current CNN models and visual Transformer models face challenges such as limited long-range modeling capabilities and high computational complexity, existing deep learning anomaly detection methods struggle to effectively perform. The state space model (SSM), represented by Mamba, excels at long-range modeling while maintaining linear computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a novel visual state space reconstruction network (HSS-UNet) for detecting CSC loosening anomalies. The network consists of a pre-trained encoder and a Mamba decoder with a multi-scale (position-enhanced state space) LSS module. The HSS block utilizes a (hybrid scan) HS encoder to encode the feature map into five scanning methods and eight orientations, thereby strengthening global connectivity through the state-space model (SSM). Finally, a stable anomaly score calculation module is designed using MLP to assess the degree of anomaly in the components. Experimental results show that the HSS-UNet model, learning strategy, and anomaly score calculation method proposed in this paper are effective and reasonable, offering certain advantages. Therefore, the method proposed can be effectively applied to the detection of CSC abnormalities.

DOI:10.1109/cspa64953.2025.10933098.abstract: Early and accurate detection of depression is critical for improving mental health outcomes. Yet, selecting an appropriate machine learning approach remains challenging due to differences in data availability, annotation costs, and computational resources. Fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) and Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) represent fundamentally distinct paradigms for natural language understanding tasks. Comparing these approaches is crucial because LLMs rely on large, labeled datasets, while ZSL provides a practical alternative in scenarios with limited or no annotated data. Despite their growing application, these methods are often studied in isolation, leaving a gap in understanding their relative advantages and trade-offs. This study addresses this gap by evaluating the performance of a fine-tuned BERT-LLM and a BART-based ZSL model on our custom-made Depression Analysis Dataset (DAD). Our research experiments showed that the fine-tuned BERT-LLM achieved accuracy and F1 scores of 98.94% and 99.24 %, respectively, while the BART-ZSL model attained 76.53% and 81.26%. The findings highlight the suitability of LLMs for high-reliability settings and ZSL for early detection in resource-constrained contexts, providing actionable insights for data scientists and mental health practitioners to design effective and accessible depression detection systems.

DOI:10.1109/cvidl70130.2026.11637509.abstract: RGB-infrared (RGB-T) pedestrian detection is a critical capability for autonomous driving and surveillance systems under diverse illumination conditions. Existing multimodal fusion approaches still suffer from three key limitations: (1) conventional fusion operators such as concatenation and elementwise addition confine cross-modal interaction to local receptive fields and fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies between distant pedestrians and scene context; (2) fusion weights remain spatially uniform across the image, although modality reliability varies markedly within a single frame-well-lit regions favor RGB texture, whereas shadowed areas require infrared thermal cues; and (3) channel-wise recalibration mechanisms based on independent sigmoid gating lack inter-channel competition, allowing redundant channels to retain high weights. To address these limitations, we propose a Selective Mamba-Fusion (SMF) module with three complementary components: (1) a Mamba Fusion Core that interleaves dual-modal channel groups and applies selective state-space scanning with $\mathcal{O}(N)$ complexity for global cross-modal interaction without cross-attention overhead; (2) an Illumination-Conditioned Modulation (ICM-FiLM) mechanism that generates spatially-varying affine transforms from RGB features to adaptively reweight the fused representation according to local lighting conditions; and (3) a Group-wise Channel Recalibration (GCR) mechanism that enforces competitive Softmax normalization across channel groups, enabling sampledependent and scale-aware routing. Experiments on LLVIP show that our method achieves a log-average miss rate of 7.28% and mAP@0.5 of 98.5%, establishing state-of-the-art performance on safety-critical detection metrics. Visualization further confirms that ICM-FiLM learns spatially selective modulation aligned with illumination boundaries, while GCR develops scale-dependent routing patterns across pyramid levels.

DOI:10.1109/cvidl70130.2026.11637833.abstract: This study addresses the four-class classification of peripheral blood smear images in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Using hue, saturation, value (HSV)-segmented cell images as input, this paper compares multiple Convolutional Neural Networks, Vision Transformer architectures, and Mamba variants under identical data partitioning and training configurations. To disentangle the effects of model architecture from the inductive bias imparted by natural image pretraining on the ImageNet dataset, experiments are conducted with random weight initialization and with fine-tuning following ImageNet pretraining. Interpretability and performance are analyzed using gradient-weighted class activation mapping, confusion matrices, receiver operating characteristic curves, and hyperparameter sensitivity assessments. After fine-tuning, EfficientFormerV2-S0 achieves 99.69% accuracy with only 3.25 million parameters, representing a favorable trade-off between accuracy and parameter efficiency. VisionMamba3 requires the shortest training time, and Mamba3 U-Net reaches 98.47% accuracy without pretraining, outperforming some transfer learning models and demonstrating greater robustness under hyperparameter perturbations. These results indicate that compact hybrid vision models can attain high recognition performance on ALL cell images segmented in color space, and that large-scale models are not the sole viable option.

DOI:10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.01181.abstract: Pansharpening aims at integrating complementary information from panchromatic and multispectral images. Available deep-learning based pansharpening methods typically perform exceptionally with particular satellite datasets. At the same time, it has been observed that these models also exhibit scene dependence, for example, if the majority of the training samples come from the urban scenes, the model’s performance may decline in the river scene. To address the domain gap produced by varying satellite sensors and distinct scenes, we propose a dual-granularity semantic guided sparse routing diffusion model for general pansharpening. By utilizing the large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in the field of geoscience, e.g, GeoChat, we introduce the dual granularity semantics to generate dynamic sparse routing scores for adaptation of different satellite sensors and scenes. This scene-level and region-level dual-granularity semantic information serves as guidance for dynamically activating specialized experts within the diffusion model. Extensive experiments on WorldView-3, QuickBird, and GaoFen-2 datasets show the effectiveness of our proposed method. Notably, the proposed method outperforms the comparison approaches in adapting to new satellite sensors and scenes. The codes are available at https://github.com/codgodtao/SGDiff.

DOI:10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.02305.abstract: Knowledge-Based visual question answering (KBVQA) separates image interpretation and knowledge retrieval into separate processes, motivated in part by the fact that they are very different tasks. In this paper, we transform the KB-VQA into linguistic question-answering tasks so that we can leverage the rich world knowledge and strong reasoning abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). The caption-then-question approach to KBVQA has been effective, but relies on the captioning method to describe the detail required to answer every possible question. We propose instead a Question-Aware Captioner (QACap), which uses the question as guidance to extract correlated visual information from the image and generate a question-related caption. To train such a model, we utilize GPT-4 to build a corresponding high-quality question-aware caption dataset on top of existing KBVQA datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our QACap model and dataset significantly improve KBVQA performance. Our method, QA-Cap, achieves 68.2% accuracy on the OKVQA validation set, 73.4% on the direct-answer part of the A-OKVQA validation set, and 74.8% on the multiple-choice part, all setting new SOTA benchmarks.

DOI:10.1109/dac63849.2025.11132528.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) technique holds significant promise for scaling up Transformer models. However, the data transfer overhead and imbalanced workload hinder efficient deployment. This work presents PIMoE, a heterogeneous system combining processing-in-memory (PIM) and neural-processing-unit (NPU) to facilitate efficient MoE Transformer inference. We propose a throttle-aware task offloading method that addresses workload imbalance between NPU and PIM, achieving optimal task distribution. Furthermore, we design a near-memory-controller data condenser to address the mismatch of sparse data layout between NPU and PIM, enhancing data transfer efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that PIMoE achieves $4.5 \times$ speedup and $13.7 \times$ greater energy efficiency compared to the A 100, and $1.4 \times$ speedup over a state-of-the-art MoE platform.

DOI:10.1109/dac63849.2025.11132800.abstract: Compute-in-memory (CiM) has become a promising candidate for edge AI by reducing data movements through insitu operations. However, this emerging computational paradigm also poses the vulnerability of model leakage as the weights are stored in plaintext for computing. While prior works have explored lightweight encryption methods, CiM is usually considered a separate module instead of a system component, leaving the origin of keys unclear and unprotected. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) offer a potential origin of keys, but a comprehensive framework for securing key generation and delivery remains lacking. Besides, the complementary ciphertext storage incurs substantial costs and degrades the performance. This work proposes PUFiM, a robust and efficient security solution for edge computing based on ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs). For the first time, a strong PUF is synergized with CiM to enable authentication, key generation, and encrypted computations within a unified array for comprehensive protection. To achieve this synergization, a high-density hybrid storage and computation approach combining PUF and weight bits via multi-level cell (MLC) FeFETs is proposed. Besides, two PUF enhancement techniques and a novel mapping scheme are developed to improve security and efficiency further. Results show that PUFiM withstands PUF modeling attacks with up to $\mathbf{1 0 M}$ samples. Moreover, PUFiM reduces the inference accuracy by $\gt 60 \%$ under 95% key leakage and achieves $\gt 9.7 \times$ compute density and $\gt 1.2 \times$ energy efficiency improvement compared with the state-of-the-art SRAM/NVM secure CiMs.

DOI:10.1109/dicta51227.2020.9363370.abstract: Due to the rapid development in robotics and autonomous industries, optimization and accuracy have become an important factor in the field of computer vision. It becomes a challenging task for the researchers to design an efficient, optimized model with high accuracy in the field of object detection and semantic segmentation. Some existing off-line scene segmentation methods have shown an outstanding result on different datasets at the cost of a large number of parameters and operations, whereas some well-known real-time semantic segmentation techniques have reduced the number of parameters and operations in demand for resource-constrained applications, but model accuracy is compromised. We propose a novel approach for scene segmentation suitable for resource-constrained embedded devices by keeping a right balance between model architecture and model performance. Exploiting the multi-scale feature fusion technique with accurate localization augmentation, we introduce a fast feature aggregation network, a real-time scene segmentation model capable of handling high-resolution input image (1024 × 2048 px). Relying on an efficient embedded vision backbone network, our feature pyramid network outperforms many existing off-line and real-time pixel-wise deep convolution neural networks (CNNs) and produces 89.7% pixel accuracy and 65.9% mean intersection over union (mIoU) on the Cityscapes benchmark validation dataset whilst having only 1.1M parameters and 5.8B FLOPS.

DOI:10.1109/ecis65594.2025.11086803.abstract: Advancements in hyperspectral remote sensing technology have significantly enhanced the capability for land cover classification. Both convolutional neural networks and transformer-based approaches have been widely adopted in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification tasks due to their powerful feature extraction capabilities. However, practical applications often face constraints due to the high cost of labeling, resulting in limited availability of accurately labeled data. Moreover, hyperspectral data requires simultaneous modeling of spatial and spectral features, and conventional approaches typically process these features types separately, which may lead to information loss during feature fusion. To tackle these challenges, we introduce an innovative Mamba-driven dynamic fusion strategy (MambaDFS) for hyperspectral and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) image classification. The proposed method leverages the dynamic weighting mechanism of Mamba to adaptively adjust the fusion weights of multimodal features, enhancing discriminative feature representation while maintaining global contextual modeling, thereby achieving high-precision classification with limited samples. Experimental results on benchmark datasets reveal that the proposed MambaDFS achieves superior results in overall accuracy, average accuracy, and Kappa coefficient compared to nine other existing methods.

DOI:10.1109/edm69524.2026.11632111.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive empirical study of the impact of quantisation schemes on small language models designed for consumer-grade hardware with strict VRAM constraints. We evaluate FP16 (baseline), INT8, AWQ (4-bit) and QLoRA (4-bit NF4) on four representative models: Mistral-7B, Phi-2 (2.7B), Qwen2.5-3B and TinyLlama (1.1B). All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA RTX 4060 laptop GPU (8 GB GDDR6). The results show that 4-bit quantisation is essential for models with parameters exceeding 3B: AWQ and QLoRA reduce VRAM usage to 4.3-5.8 GB (compared to 14+ GB in FP16), enabling full VRAM output without offloading. This yields 2-4 times higher generation throughput (up to 410.91 tokens/s) with negligible accuracy degradation on BoolQ (0.70-0.71), GSM8k (drop $\leq 7 \%$) and Hellaswag (0.12-0.39 across models and schemes). INT8 offers only minor memory savings and suffers from high dequantisation costs on modern GPUs, making it sub-optimal. The study highlights that AWQ is the best compromise between quality, speed and memory for edge deployment. Our results offer practical recommendations for deploying SLMs on laptops and portable devices as of 2026.

DOI:10.1109/eibdct69742.2026.11566909.abstract: Accurate electricity price forecasting is critical for market participants and grid operators in deregulated power markets. However, existing methods face three challenges: (1) the coexistence of smooth macro-trends and volatile micro-oscillations demands heterogeneous modeling capacity, (2) abrupt price spikes interspersed within regular diurnal cycles require selective information propagation across different temporal scales, and (3) quadratic-complexity attention mechanisms limit scalability to long prediction horizons. We propose DecompSSM, a dual-path framework with three innovations: (1) an Adaptive Decomposition Gateway (ADG) that separates input signals into trend and seasonal streams, (2) a Selective State Space Seasonal Encoder (S4E) with input-dependent discretization to adaptively control temporal resolution, and (3) an additive Dual-Path Fusion mechanism that recombines heterogeneous representations with linear complexity. Experiments on a seven-year real-world electricity market dataset demonstrate that DecompSSM outperforms nine baselines across all horizons, achieving up to 6.6% MSE reduction while maintaining linear computational complexity.

DOI:10.1109/eicars71536.2026.11694530.abstract: Pseudo changes caused by illumination, seasonal variations, and slight misregistration remain a challenge in remote sensing change detection. This paper presents a spatialconsistency-guided heat-diffusion network. A shared-weight vHeat encoder uses Heat2D to model local details and long-range dependencies, while a spatial-consistency-guided heat conduction operator (SC-HCO) module generates difference-guided spatial weights to suppress unreliable responses. A multi-scale decoder fuses bi-temporal features with absolute differences to recover complete change regions. On LEVIR-CD, UAV-CD, and SYSUCD, the method achieves F1/IoU scores of 91.40%/84.16%, 76.22%/61.58%, and 83.29%/71.37%, respectively.

DOI:10.1109/eicct69950.2026.11564635.abstract: Early and precise grading of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is of great clinical significance for preventing vision loss. While existing CNN-Mamba hybrid models have shown promise in automated screening, there remains room for improvement in preserving fine-grained lesion details and resolving semantic conflicts during cross-branch feature fusion. To address this, we propose ResMamba, a dual-branch architecture combining ResNet-50 for local feature extraction and Mamba for global context modeling. We introduce a Lesion-Aware Cross-Scanning mechanism to mitigate signal dilution, a Discrepancy-Driven Mutual-Aware Dual Gate (MADGate) to smoothly resolve semantic conflicts, and a Multi-Constraint Hybrid Loss (MCHL) to better align with the monotonic progression of the disease. Experimental results on public datasets indicate that ResMamba effectively improves the Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) metric, demonstrating reliable clinical diagnostic consistency by penalizing severe cross-grade misclassifications.

DOI:10.1109/estream61684.2024.10542617.abstract: The recent advancements in neural network architectures, particularly transformers, have played a crucial role in the rapid progress of Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are trained on many parameters. By training these parameters on vast amounts of text data, LLMs can learn to generate reactions to a wide variety of prompts. These models have enabled machines to generate new data (human-like), driving significant developments in Natural Language Processing (NLP). They have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in producing new content. Besides their impressive performance, LLMs occasionally generate hallucinatory responses that produce nonsensical or inaccurate information. In simple terms, hallucinations in LLMs happen when the model generates information that may sound believable but is actually wrong. It can make up details or go beyond what it has learned from the training data, resulting in inaccurate output. These hallucinatory responses appear to be authentic but lack grounding in reality. Such hallucinations can include fabrications such as facts, events, or statements that lack support from real-world data. Addressing this issue is important to enhance the reliability of AI-generated content. Hallucinations can be a significant challenge in critical applications such as healthcare, law, etc. In this view, this paper delves into the phenomenon of hallucinations in the context of LLMs. The objective is to understand the causes, explore the implications, and discuss potential strategies for mitigation.

DOI:10.1109/fccm68464.2026.00050.abstract: THE growing integration of Transformer-based artificial intelligence (AI) agents into core operating system functions is a key driver in modern laptop systems-on-chip (SoCs) design. While enabling powerful capabilities, their inference incurs significant compute and data-movement overhead, making them highly energy-intensive. This energy cost is a fundamental bottleneck for embedded mobile platforms with tight power and thermal constraints [2] . The Attention prefill stage is a major contributor to inference latency and energy at long sequence lengths. Consequently, significant effort has focused on optimizing attention across commercial [3] and academic platforms [4] , spanning algorithmic advances such as FlashAttention [3] and hardware enhancements including specialized non-linear units. Neural processing units (NPUs) achieve high energy efficiency through spatial dataflow architectures and explicit data-movement programming models, which expose fine-grained control over computation and memory transfers. While extensive prior work has focused on optimizing attention for graphics processing units (GPUs), comparatively few efforts have targeted attention for NPUs.

DOI:10.1109/fllm67465.2025.11391055.abstract: Generative large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across a wide range of natural language processing tasks. Building on this progress, there is growing interest in extending such capabilities to speech-based interaction—an essential and natural form of human communication with broad real-world applications. Speech LLMs require more than modular extensions to existing text-based architectures; they demand specialized, unified designs that address the unique challenges of the speech modality, such as acoustic variability, audio data scarcity, and cross-modal alignment challenges. In this survey, we systematically review training strategies for developing Speech LLMs, organizing them into three key stages: pretraining, fine-tuning, and post-training alignment. Through an analysis of recent models and methods, we present a structured taxonomy of these strategies, highlighting current limitations, open research questions, and future directions to guide the development of robust, efficient, and well-aligned Speech LLMs for real-world deployment.
